# Baudrillard — The Transparency of Evil (1990)

## Bibliographic identity

French original: *La Transparence du mal: essai sur les phénomènes extrêmes* (Paris: Galilée, 1990). The [consulted primary preview](https://pdfcoffee.com/baudrillard-the-transparency-of-evil-essays-on-extreme-phenomena-1993-pdf-free.html) reproduces title/copyright and contents identifying James Benedict's 1993 Verso translation. “After the Orgy” starts at printed p.3. The browser tool exposes the primary text; direct download returned 403, so no complete local scan is claimed.

**Full note:** Jean Baudrillard, *The Transparency of Evil: Essays on Extreme Phenomena*, trans. James Benedict (London: Verso, 1993), 3–6.

**Shortened note:** Baudrillard, *The Transparency of Evil*, page.

**Bibliography:** Baudrillard, Jean. *The Transparency of Evil: Essays on Extreme Phenomena*. Translated by James Benedict. London: Verso, 1993.

## Source scholarship

The opening asks what follows the realised liberations of modernity. Continued reproduction can outlive its purposes; the fractal account then distinguishes dispersal from the earlier laws of value. It explicitly removes equivalence, rather than completing universal convertibility. Natural/use, commodity/exchange and structural/sign stages precede the proposed fractal stage; this is a value-stage account, distinct from both the image phases and historical orders.

The essay's transparency-without-trust comparison remains operationally useful, but the precise visibility passage is now independently located in Forget Foucault pp.36–40. This house does not borrow that passage under a new title.

## Superseded intake and retained research

The old q001 generic-obscenity lead is superseded by the precisely located orgy passage; the visibility research route survives in Forget Foucault q003. Former q003 Perfect Crime is an unverified separate 1995-work lead, not an admitted passage here. The fractal-as-total-convertibility account is withdrawn. Prakāśa-without-vimarśa and perfect-crime/cohomology remain unratified comparisons, not sourced doctrinal identities.

## Open acquisition and verification

Acquire and visually collate the 1993 volume for quotations and read the remaining essays before making whole-volume claims. Preserve radical-otherness chapters as distinct future research. Empirical transparency/trust effects need actual cases; no theorem that cohomology is always nonzero follows from these sources.
